items.context: @AshCrypto (2.148.691 seguidores), en inglés, con imagen: «Bitcoin Weekly Update: 7 consecutive red weekly candles... BTC dumped to a new low of $55,130... Resistance: 200-week MA near $68,363 and 50-week MA near $74,000. Is the bottom in? It's still too early to say.» Post de ~16 min con 93 likes, 10 reposts, 22 respuestas y 25.056 vistas. Ángulo: precio bajo la media de 200 semanas = lectura fría; su Market Temperature combina MVRV, 200W, caída desde el máximo y momentum (99,29→0,67 en 364 días).
items.suggested_text:
Seven straight red weekly candles with price still under the 200-week MA is a stretch that reads cold, not hot. Price vs the 200W is a slow gauge: it doesn't call the exact bottom, it tells you how stretched the market is against its multi-year average.

That's why it works better next to MVRV, the drawdown from the high and volatility-adjusted momentum than on its own. My Market Temperature index blends those four at 25% each, and it went from 99.29 to 0.67 in 364 days.

A cold reading has never been a timing signal by itself. What it changes is the asymmetry, and that's where most of the "is the bottom in" debate actually lives.
